name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,208

clue.text: Village play

blocks.note: first meaning: a small settlement, smaller than a village
second meaning: Shakespeare's tragedy about the Prince of Denmark

explanation.walkthrough: Two words, two meanings: the surface hints at amateur village theatre, but each word separately defines the same answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamlet is a tiny rural settlement, and Hamlet is also the title of Shakespeare's famous tragedy.

clue.text: Maybe nag can be heard speaking roughly?

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for an adjective

indicators.note: what can be heard is judged by sound, so a word that sounds the same is wanted

blocks.note: a nag is an old horse; 'Maybe' marks it as an example

explanation.surface: A nagging person whose voice has gone rough from all the complaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nag' looks like a person who scolds, but here it is an old horse, an example flagged by 'Maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoarse voice is rough and croaky, so someone hoarse sounds harsh when talking.

clue.text: Facing in, aim to develop enlargement

indicators.note: developing something changes its shape, so these letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; also part of the indicator phrase in the surface

explanation.surface: Advice to turn inward and aim at self-improvement and growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' does double duty: it is fodder and also reads as part of 'to develop'.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnification is the act of making something appear larger, which is exactly an enlargement.

clue.text: Famous rapper, mostly not without heart

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
a thing without its heart has lost its central letter

blocks.note: Eminem is the famous US rapper, cut short
the word with its middle letter removed

explanation.surface: A well-known rapper described as mostly lacking heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Famous rapper' reads as one phrase, but 'Famous' is the definition and the rapper is Eminem.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent means distinguished and well known in a field, a close synonym for renowned.

clue.text: Endlessly trod grassy plain

indicators.note: something endless has had its end removed, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: the past tense of walk with feet, minus its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone walking on and on across a wide grassland.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb 'trod' becomes STEPPED, and losing the final D leaves the plain.
explanation.definitionFit: A steppe is a vast treeless grassland, especially in Eastern Europe and Central Asia.

clue.text: Musical work: NY opera company raised its speed?

indicators.note: in a down answer, raising letters means reading them bottom to top

blocks.note: op. is short for opus, a numbered musical work
the Met is New York's Metropolitan Opera

explanation.surface: A New York opera company speeding up its performance of a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its' points back to the musical work, so the definition is the speed of that work.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempo is the pace at which a piece of music is played, its rate of beats.

clue.text: Frantic, disorderly span in cricket

indicators.note: something disorderly is out of its proper order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wild, chaotic stretch of play in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorderly' looks like it describes the frantic span, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone panic-stricken is overwhelmed by fear and acting wildly, which is frantic behaviour.

clue.text: Not all of scribes say something in writings on a subject

indicators.note: taking not all of a stretch of words means only a part of their letters is used

blocks.note: the letters run across the word boundaries

explanation.surface: Some writers have something to say in their compositions.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans the end of 'scribes', all of 'say' and the start of 'something'.
explanation.definitionFit: Essays are short prose compositions that discuss a particular topic or argument.

clue.text: Extreme misery of USA, nigh exploding

indicators.note: an explosion scatters pieces, so these letters land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Deep distress in America as it seems close to blowing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nigh' means near; its letters join those of USA as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Anguish is severe mental or physical suffering, a word for great distress and pain.

clue.text: Under cooking surface, almost lose ability to see mischievous creature

indicators.note: in a down answer, what is under comes below, so one part follows the other
almost means not quite, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a hob is the top of a stove where pans sit
to lose sight is to go blind, without its last letter

explanation.surface: Something beneath the stove that nearly blinds you turns out to be an imp.
explanation.walkthrough: A hob is the British word for a stovetop. GO BLIND, cut short, sits below it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobgoblin is a small, impish sprite of folklore that plays tricks on people.

clue.text: Take away menus with second item replaced by starter for Indian

indicators.note: replacing the second item means swapping out the letter in position two
a starter is what comes first, so only an opening letter is used

blocks.note: taken as written; its E is the one to swap
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A takeaway's menus, with a dish swapped for an Indian appetiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take away' and 'starter' borrow restaurant language, but the definition means subtract. The E of MENUS gives way to I.
explanation.definitionFit: Minus is the arithmetic word for subtract, as in five minus two.

clue.text: Some players win, especially a scoundrel

indicators.note: some of a phrase is only a part of it, so a run of its letters is wanted

blocks.note: the letters run across the word boundaries

explanation.surface: Some players come out on top, notably a rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans the last letter of 'players', all of 'win' and the first of 'especially'.
explanation.definitionFit: Swine is an insult for a contemptible, nasty person, a rogue or villain.

clue.text: Disguised by cloth with irregular patches of colour

indicators.note: a disguise changes how something looks, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something camouflaged by a fabric covered in uneven coloured splotches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disguised by' reads as one phrase, but 'by' belongs with 'cloth' as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotchy skin or fabric is marked with uneven spots or smudges of different shades.

clue.text: Popular time traveller beginning to trust self-absorbed person

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that is taken

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
T is the abbreviation for time
a rover is a wanderer
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A well-liked time traveller starting to trust someone wrapped up in themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time traveller' reads as one science-fiction figure, but time and traveller give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An introvert turns attention inward and prefers solitude, so is focused on their own inner world.

clue.text: Show former partner Hello! piece

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
a greeting
a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: Display an ex-partner's article in Hello!, the celebrity magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Hello! looks like the gossip magazine, but it is just a greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhibit is to put on display or reveal, so it is a verb synonym for display.

clue.text: Scratches small restraints on wrists

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
handcuffs, shortened

explanation.surface: Tight little handcuffs leave marks on someone's wrists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scratches' reads as a noun describing the marks; it works as a verb or noun equally.
explanation.definitionFit: Scuffs are marks made by scraping or rubbing a surface, so they are light scrapes.

clue.text: Wonder who sings — that is after send-up of animal doctors

indicators.note: in a down answer, sending something up means reading it bottom to top
one thing coming after another places it later in the answer

blocks.note: vets treat animals
i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: Wondering who is singing in a comic sketch about vets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wonder' looks like a verb, but it is the surname of the singer Stevie Wonder; the definition is his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The singer-songwriter Stevie Wonder is known by this first name, so it identifies the Wonder who performs.

clue.text: Combustible rock covering a street beside the sea

indicators.note: to cover something is to wrap around it, so one piece goes outside another

blocks.note: coal is a rock that burns
taken as written
St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Burning rock spread over a road by the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Combustible rock' is a cryptic way of naming a fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Coastal describes places at or near the shore, where land meets ocean.

clue.text: As of old, your meal’s half herb

indicators.note: half of a word keeps only part of it, so two of its letters go

blocks.note: thy is the archaic form of your
the first half of the word

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned remark that half of your dinner is seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As of old' tells the solver to use the archaic word for your.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is a fragrant culinary plant whose leaves season food.

clue.text: Lift up one among many

indicators.note: something among others sits in their midst, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: a host is a great number
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Raising a single person above a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one among many' sounds like an idiom, but it is a placement instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist is to raise something, often with ropes or tackle, so it means to raise.

clue.text: “Magic” being just technology in the end

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is taken

blocks.note: just means fair
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A claim that magic is really just advanced technology.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'being' look like a verb; it is a noun, a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairy is a small supernatural creature of folklore with enchanted powers.

clue.text: Russian-born author reversed vehicle across trashed book

indicators.note: reversing means going backwards, so the letters are read right to left
something trashed is wrecked, so these letters are jumbled
lying across something spans it, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: a van is a vehicle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer backing a van over a ruined book.
explanation.walkthrough: Vladimir Nabokov, author of Lolita, was born in St Petersburg.
explanation.definitionFit: Nabokov was a novelist born in Russia who later wrote in English.

clue.text: Star role in Barbie is below the usual level

blocks.note: the sun is a star
Ken is Barbie's boyfriend, a part in the Barbie film

explanation.surface: A star's part in the Barbie movie is beneath their usual standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' looks like a famous actor, but it is the astronomical star.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunken means lying lower than the surrounding surface, as in a sunken garden.

clue.text: Lots joining Anglican church simultaneously

indicators.note: joining means attaching, so one part is placed next to the other

blocks.note: a ton of something means lots of it
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: Many people signing up to the Church of England together.
explanation.walkthrough: The Church of England is England's Anglican church, abbreviated CE.
explanation.definitionFit: At once can mean all together at the same moment, as in everyone spoke at once.
